solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A bouquet may give such a lift

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its scent or aroma

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers might cheer someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like a lift to the spirits; it is a rise or climb.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift is an upward movement, a climb or rise.

clue.text: I get married and set out full of beans!

indicators.note: set out round, the word and is laid open on either side of the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
to mate is to pair up or wed

explanation.surface: A newlywed sets off on honeymoon brimming with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' is a container signal here: the word 'and' is spread open to hold the rest, rather than meaning departing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of beans is lively and spirited, exactly a synonym.

clue.text: Fish needs to join chips

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
to enter a club or race is to join it

explanation.surface: Fish and chips go together on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' is the traditional British nickname for a woodworker, as in 'Chippy'; nothing to do with fried potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips is a long-standing British nickname for a woodworker who makes joinery.

clue.text: Cattle without water

definitions.meaning: an old word for oxen or cows, as in neatherd
a spirit served undiluted, with nothing added

explanation.surface: Livestock left in a drought with nothing to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic English uses this word for bovine stock; and a whisky taken straight has no water added.

clue.text: Worn by soldiers for cleaning drains?

definitions.meaning: army working dress, plain combat clothing
menial camp chores given to troops, such as scrubbing gutters, are called by this name

explanation.surface: Army clothing designed for the dirty job of unblocking drains.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both military work uniform and the menial duties soldiers are set.

clue.text: Allocated as indicated

parts.note: taken as written
signed means indicated by a gesture or signpost

explanation.surface: Duties were handed out just as the notice said.
explanation.definitionFit: Something allocated has been allotted or given out to someone, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Where coffees are served and drunk

definitions.meaning: taken literally, coffee comes in mugs or small bowls

explanation.surface: A café scene where people are both served and drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being tipsy also literally describes coffee sitting in its crockery.

clue.text: One accepts student as dim

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one
L is the learner plate, a student driver

explanation.surface: A single pupil who is a bit slow on the uptake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim' suggests stupidity; here it means unilluminated.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim room has no lamps burning, so it is dark.

clue.text: Presumably he likes painstaking people

parts.note: read painstaking as pain-taking: someone who enjoys inflicting suffering

explanation.surface: A man who admires conscientious, careful workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'painstaking' into 'pains taking': a person who likes taking pains from others is a cruel one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes pleasure in hurting others relishes giving pain.

clue.text: Where ladies wear new hats and new coats

indicators.note: new describes the word coats made over into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Fashionable women show off fresh hats and coats at a social event.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is the English racecourse whose Royal meeting is famous for extravagant ladies' hats.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berkshire racecourse is famed for its Ladies' Day millinery parade.

clue.text: Hostile incursions into Greek island, say?

parts.note: taken as in

indicators.note: say tells us the island's name is spoken, giving a word sounding like it

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: Raiders invading a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Making inroads means advancing into enemy territory, raids or incursions.

clue.text: Rotten pie sold in error

indicators.note: in error says the letters of pie sold are set down wrongly, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A bad pie was sold by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone rotten has gone off or become inedible.

clue.text: Third man sounds competent

indicators.note: sounds means the word for competent is spoken, giving a name with the same sound

parts.note: able means capable or competent

explanation.surface: The third person in line seems capable.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, after Adam and Eve, Abel was the third human.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblically, Adam's second son was the third person to exist after his parents.

clue.text: Glasses with handles, other than tankards

definitions.text: Glasses with handles, other than tankards

parts.words: Glasses with handles, other than tankards
parts.note: glasses here are spectacles, not drinking vessels, held up on a stick

explanation.surface: Drinking glasses with handles that are not beer mugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glasses with handles' first suggests beer mugs; the clue rules them out to point to eyewear.
explanation.definitionFit: These are opera spectacles held to the eyes by a long handle.

clue.text: Nocturnal creature needing regular transfusions

parts.note: a night-flying mammal that feeds on blood, as if needing a top-up of it

explanation.surface: A night animal that is ill and needs blood treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American flying mammal lives by drinking the blood of other animals at night.

clue.text: Take some back to quarters

indicators.note: to means attached to, so the reversed piece is joined onto the end of the compass points

parts.note: E and N are two compass quarters, east and north

indicators.note: back says the word for some is read from right to left

parts.note: part means some of something

explanation.surface: Bring a few items back to living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal, not a return journey; 'quarters' means compass points, not lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a criminal is to capture or catch him, as in a snare.

clue.text: Classical admission of guilt

parts.note: Latin, the classical language, for I have sinned

explanation.definitionFit: A Latin confession meaning I have sinned, used jokingly in English.

clue.text: Place for watching TV? It's a matter of opinion

definitions.meaning: a spot to watch from; TV is read as a view
a stance or perspective one holds

explanation.surface: Where you sit to watch television is down to personal taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a vantage spot for looking out and a personal outlook.

clue.text: It strengthens the wall, still needs a lock

parts.note: but in the sense of nevertheless, still
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A wall needs reinforcement yet also a padlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A masonry support built against a wall props and strengthens it.

clue.text: Unnecessary to curtail one's requirements

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ..., wanting fewer things

explanation.surface: Cutting back on what one wants is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncalled-for is not wanted; split in two, the word says want fewer.

clue.text: Unusually proud to make a fresh start at Rugby

definitions.text: make a fresh start at Rugby

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of proud and to are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: A boastful pupil starts afresh at Rugby School.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby suggests the public school; it is the game, where a drop-out restarts play with a drop kick from the 22-metre line.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union a restart kick taken from the defending 22 is called by this name.

clue.text: A bit for each

parts.note: a piece is a bit or portion

explanation.surface: Handing out a little to every person.
explanation.definitionFit: Priced individually, per item, as in a pound per item.

clue.text: Wine container under the counter

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the container piece below the counter piece

parts.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
a sac is a pouch or bag in anatomy

explanation.surface: A bottle of wine hidden beneath the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white Bordeaux from the Sauternes district shares this village name.

clue.text: Articulate deputy admits nothing

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: vice as in vice-president, a deputy
O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: An eloquent second-in-command confesses to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate a thought is to express or utter it in words.

clue.text: Change the blend of tea on trial

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters of tea on trial are mixed

explanation.surface: Try out a different tea blend.
explanation.definitionFit: A modification or adjustment is a change to something.

clue.text: A capital decoration for the Pope

definitions.text: A capital decoration for the Pope

parts.words: A capital decoration for the Pope
parts.note: capital in the sense of for the head: a papal triple crown

explanation.surface: A splendid ornament fit for the pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like 'excellent' or a city; it means of the head (Latin caput).
explanation.definitionFit: The papal triple crown is a jewelled headdress worn by popes.

clue.text: One's pedometer shows how one went fast

indicators.note: shows means the letters are on display within the words one's pedometer

explanation.surface: A step counter reveals how quickly someone walked.
explanation.definitionFit: To have moved quickly or hurried is past tense of a verb for speed.

clue.text: Point a primate out in church

indicators.note: out means outside, so the primate piece goes around the point

parts.note: an ape is a primate
S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone indicates an ape in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop in a church; it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church building.

clue.text: Drag one's feet in quiet stroll

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
to amble is to stroll

explanation.surface: Dawdling along on a peaceful walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk awkwardly and shuffle along is to move with dragging feet.

clue.text: The top cereal — fancy!

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: An exclamation over the finest breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim or sudden notion is a passing fancy.

clue.text: It's back in the race to beat one

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a chase is a race, as in the steeplechase

indicators.note: back means the letters of it's are read in reverse

parts.note: the letters of it's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Coming last in the race means you'll be thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses IT'S (apostrophe ignored) to give STI; a steeplechase is a race, hence chase.
explanation.definitionFit: To punish physically, especially by thrashing, is to beat.

clue.text: New arrivals, we hear, at the docks

indicators.note: we hear means the word for new arrivals is spoken, matching another spelling

parts.note: births are new babies arriving

explanation.surface: Newcomers reported arriving at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorings for ships, places where vessels tie up in harbour.
